Eurogroup Laminations SpA Announces €60 Million Expansion to Boost Production Capacity

Eurogroup Laminations SpA, a leading manufacturer in Italy’s machinery sector, has unveiled plans for a €60 million investment aimed at expanding its production facilities in the Lombardy region. The initiative is set to increase the company’s output of electric motor laminations, a key component in the rapidly growing electric mobility and industrial automation markets.

In a statement released on Thursday, Eurogroup Laminations SpA said the expansion will add 15,000 square meters to its existing plant in Baranzate, north of Milan, and is expected to be fully operational by the third quarter of 2025. The company anticipates the project will create up to 120 new skilled jobs in the region, reinforcing its commitment to local employment and technological innovation.

“This investment underlines our confidence in the long-term growth potential of the electrification sector,” said CEO Gianluca Bisol. “We are seeing robust demand from both the automotive and industrial segments, and this expansion will allow us to serve our clients even more effectively, while supporting the region’s economic development.”

Industry analysts have welcomed the move, citing strong tailwinds for suppliers of electric motor components. “The transition to electric vehicles and automation continues to drive demand for high-precision laminations,” commented Alessia Conti, machinery sector analyst at Milan-based research firm ItalTrade Insights. “Eurogroup Laminations’ expansion demonstrates its strategic focus and positions it to capture further market share as electrification accelerates across Europe.”

The expansion is expected to enhance the company’s manufacturing flexibility, with upgraded machinery and production lines designed for higher efficiency and reduced environmental impact. According to the company, the new facility will incorporate advanced recycling systems to minimize material waste, as well as energy-saving technologies in line with Italy’s national sustainability targets.

Local officials expressed support for the project, highlighting its potential impact on the regional economy. “Eurogroup Laminations’ investment is a testament to Lombardy’s strength as a hub for advanced manufacturing,” said Giovanni Rizzi, regional councillor for economic development. “We look forward to seeing the positive effects on jobs, innovation, and the local supply chain.”

The company’s shares closed up 2.1% on Thursday following the announcement.
